items.title: Item 1
items.text: Snowflake Soars On Q1, AWS Deal *********************************** Snowflake (NYSE:SNOW ) popped close to 35% in pre-market trading, after first-quarter revenue jumped 34% to beat guidance – powered by gains in customer expansion and product adoption. Over 13,600 accounts adopted Snowflake’s AI-driven capabilities, with more than 7,100 using new platform features like Cortex Code for enterprise AI tasks, pushing product revenue to a new high. * New multi-year $6 billion deal with Amazon Web Services (AWS): On the same day, the company announced an agreement to access Amazon’s (NASDAQ:AMZN ) Graviton compute and AI services, more than doubling its prior commitments – as CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said Snowflake has “surpassed $7 billion in lifetime AWS Marketplace sales.” * Recommended in recent years by both Team Rule Breakers and Team Hidden Gems: Management raised its guidance, citing strong momentum in AI and enterprise partnerships – and now expects full-year revenue to reach $5.84 billion, up $180 million from its previous target. Learn how Snowflake partnered with AWS -----------------------------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 2
items.text: What You Might’ve Missed Yesterday from Team Rule Breakers’ Recs ----------------------------------------------------------------- * Braze (NASDAQ:BRZE ) delivered a 30% increase in Q1 revenue . The company’s AI-powered customer engagement platform saw a rise in new customers and higher usage among existing customers. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $895–$899 million. The stock dropped about 8% in early trading, as earnings came in flat. * Synopsys (NASDAQ:SNPS ) – recommended by both Team Hidden Gems and Team Rule Breakers – dipped around 2% early this morning, despite a Q2 revenue beat , up 42% YoY. GAAP EPS fell 96% as a result of one-off costs, though non-GAAP EPS only slipped 8.7%. * Everpure (NYSE:P ) – recommended in Stock Advisor by Team RB – posted a 35% Q1 sales rise year over year (YoY) to $1.05 billion. But the stock lost more than 8% in morning trading on the back of weaker Q2 guidance. Fool analyst Emily Flippen previously said “[Everpure] is still in the process of trying to change investor perceptions away from it being a hardware storage vendor but rather a true memory and infrastructure platform.” Read Emily’s take on Everpure's changes ----------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 3
items.text: Fed Facing Inflation, Interest Rate Dilemma ---------------------------------------------- The April Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) print – expected to show a 3.8% rise YoY – is due today, as inflation rises high on the Federal Reserve’s priorities list. Fed Governor Lisa Cook yesterday commented “I currently believe that the right course of action is to hold rates steady,” but said she’s prepared for a hike if tariffs, the Iran war, and the AI surge continue to fuel price rises. * “I don’t regret dissenting at that meeting, because the inflation has not proved as temporary as was advertised”: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee – who voted against the Fed’s final 2025 cut – warned of the risk of “big increases in consumer spending fueled by stock market wealth increases.” * Futures down as oil remains above $90 per barrel: S&P 500 futures dipped 0.1% in early trading, and Nasdaq futures lost 0.3%, as renewed strikes on Iran dampened hopes for falling oil prices. See how energy affects inflation ************************************************************

items.title: Item 4
items.text: Results From COST, ADSK, and OKTA Due After Today’s Close ************************************************************ * Costco (NASDAQ:COST ) reveals Q3 performance following a 9% YoY net sales increase in Q2 – though membership growth was slowing. A Stock Advisor rec by Team Hidden Gems, Costco is looking to build on Q2’s 22.6% rise in digitally enabled comparable sales YoY. * Autodesk (NASDAQ:ADSK ), recommended by Team Rule Breakers, opens fiscal 2027 following an expectations-beating final quarter for fiscal 2026. Q4 was hit by restructuring costs, and further impacts could be felt in the latest quarter. * Okta (NASDAQ:OKTA ) – an SA rec by Team RB – is expected to show progress with AI agent security products in Q1 today. Management expects 9% total revenue growth and 10% subscription revenue growth in the quarter. Get the lowdown on the two sides of Okta *****************************************

items.title: Item 5
items.text: Today’s Take: From Skeptic to Believer ***************************************** Yasser El-Shimy I confess, I was initially skeptical about investing in Netflix (NASDAQ:NFLX ). The streaming wars seemed destined to erode margins, with content costs spiraling whether producing originals or licensing. I questioned how they could sustain profitability amidst such intense competition. However, Netflix systematically proved me wrong. — YASSER EL-SHIMY • TEAM RULE BREAKERS Matt Frankel I’ll admit I got the buy now, pay later (BNPL) business wrong, especially with Sezzle (NASDAQ:SEZL ). A few years ago, when Affirm (NASDAQ:AFRM ) went public, I thought its loans were extremely risky, and we’d see massive defaults as soon as we had any economic weakness. Well, we did in 2022/2023, and it didn’t happen. — MATT FRANKEL • TEAM HIDDEN GEMS Here’s a sneak preview, but head to the article to share the moment you realized a stock you were skeptical of was actually a great business – and what changed your mind – or to submit questions to any of the featured analysts today! See more in Today’s Take **************

items.title: Item 6
items.text: Your Take ************** YESTERDAY'S TOP RESPONSE We asked, what's one stock, sector, or trend you're watching more closely heading into next month? A Member aredsoxfan1 said “Enphase Energy (NASDAQ:ENPH ), I've been holding and/or buying for 3 years now. I believe in the company and have always thought they will turn it around. But I am a bit puzzled by the abrupt turn the stock has taken in the last month on what I see as very little news. Is the big turn really just because they released a product that can be used by data centers? I'll be curious to find out.” See more great answers from our Foolish community TODAY’S QUESTION BBB Foods (NYSE:TBBB ) was another to report after the market closed Wednesday , with the stock down around 3.5% in pre-market trading. The discount grocer posted a steep net loss, but operating cash flow was strong (up 64%) due to its business model. When cash generation and reported earnings tell different stories, which do you trust more? How do you evaluate 'real' profitability? Elaborate in the comments on today’s article!
